name: Mercedes-AMG GT3
hook: In its first full season it won the Nürburgring 24 Hours by 5.697 seconds, the closest finish in the race's history.
story: Twenty-four hours, and it came down to one lap. The 2016 race at the Nürburgring had already been strange. Hail hit less than an hour in and turned the Nordschleife into an ice rink. The red flag stayed out for roughly four hours. When it went green again, four Mercedes-AMG GT3s settled into the front of the field and stayed there, through the night and through the morning. On the final lap Maro Engel sat behind Christian Hohenadel, who was driving the same car in different colours. Engel went past. The gap at the flag was 5.697 seconds, the closest finish the race had ever had. Behind those two came two more of the same car. First, second, third and fourth, in the first full season this model ever raced. And in the winning seat, sharing with Engel, Adam Christodoulou and Manuel Metzger, was Bernd Schneider. He was 51.
description: The Mercedes-AMG GT3 is a customer racing car: built by AMG, sold to private teams, and raced by them all over the world. It replaced the SLS AMG GT3 for 2016 and kept that car's engine, a naturally aspirated 6.2-litre V8 badged 6.3, at a moment when almost every rival had turned to turbochargers. Its road-going namesake uses a twin-turbo 4.0 instead. The racer is an aluminium spaceframe with carbon bodywork, rear-wheel drive, and a sequential six-speed gearbox mounted at the back.
